guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 16
MAJOR SCALE FOUR-NOTE ROLLING SEQUENCE - ONE-OCTAVE NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Turn the compact one-octave major scale into overlapping four-note groups. Complete the full
40-note up/down rolling cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb frame exactly
one fret, and repeat through every major key. Begin with A major at low-E fret 5, climb to
A major at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
WHY THIS LEVEL RETURNS TO ONE OCTAVE
Level 15 expanded the three-note sequence across two octaves and all six strings. Level 16
deliberately returns to the compact three-string octave so the new four-note overlap can be
learned without simultaneously managing the upper-octave B-string offset. Level 17 can extend
this exact sequence across the complete two-octave frame.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A major is the starting rung, not the
key of every rung. A fixed-key A-major exercise in every neck position requires changing the
note layout and remains a separate branch.
MAJOR-SCALE FORMULA
Degrees: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
Intervals: whole - whole - half - whole - whole - whole - half
COMPACT ONE-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
A string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4
D string:     R-1, R+1, R+2        Fingers 1,3,4
The four-fret hand frame runs from R-1 through R+2.
ROLLING FOUR-NOTE SEQUENCE
Each new group begins one scale degree farther along. At each group boundary, the line drops
a diatonic third and then continues forward. Three notes overlap from one group to the next.
Do not pause, accent, or reset at a group boundary.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
The complete up/down cell contains 10 groups and 40 notes. The octave root is repeated at the
turn: the last note of 5-6-7-8 is followed by the first note of 8-7-6-5. Because 40 is even,
the next key begins with the same pick orientation. Because every group has four notes, every
group also begins with the same stroke.
D-start groups: D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U ... through all 10 groups.
U-start groups: U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D ... through all 10 groups.
Never restart the pick cycle at a new group, string crossing, scale turn, or one-fret shift.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Use sixteenth notes: one four-note group per beat. Begin at roughly 75 percent of your clean
Level 15 metronome setting; for example, if Level 15 is clean at 80 BPM, begin near 60 BPM.
Master the A-major cell alone, then use 2-3 neighboring rungs and pause one beat after each
40-note cell. During the pause, release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat
with both pick starts. Then remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return
to fret 5. Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, an uneven
group pulse, dragged shift noise, a crossing accent, or rising tension. Advance after the full
route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 17
MAJOR SCALE FOUR-NOTE ROLLING SEQUENCE - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Extend the Level 16 four-note rolling sequence across the complete two-octave, six-string
major-scale frame. Complete the 96-note up/down cell, release pressure, move the entire
hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret, and repeat through every major key. Begin with A major
at low-E fret 5, climb to A major at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
WHAT CHANGES FROM LEVEL 16
Level 16 taught the four-note overlap inside the compact one-octave frame. Level 17 keeps the
same overlap and extends it through positions 1-15 across all six strings. This adds the middle
octave, additional string crossings, the B-string tuning offset, and a longer uninterrupted
pick cycle without changing the underlying four-note sequence rule.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A major is the starting rung, not the
key of every rung. The route passes through all 12 major keys before reaching A one octave
higher on the neck.
MAJOR-SCALE FORMULA
Intervals: whole - whole - half - whole - whole - whole - half, repeated through two octaves
TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4                 Degrees 1,2
A string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4               Degrees 3,4,5
D string:     R-1, R+1, R+2        Fingers 1,3,4               Degrees 6,7,8
G string:     R-1, R+1, R+2        Fingers 1,3,4               Degrees 9,10,11
B string:     R, R+2               Fingers 2,4                 Degrees 12,13
High e:       R-1, R               Fingers 1,2                 Degrees 14,15
The four-fret hand frame runs from R-1 through R+2.
ROLLING FOUR-NOTE SEQUENCE
ASCENDING:
DESCENDING:
Each new group begins one scale degree farther along. Three notes overlap from one group to
the next. At the boundary, the line drops a diatonic third and resumes forward motion. Do not
pause, accent, or reset at a group boundary.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
The complete up/down cell contains 24 groups and 96 notes. The high root is repeated at the
turn: the last note of 12-13-14-15 is followed by the first note of 15-14-13-12. Because 96
is even, the next key begins with the same pick orientation. Because each group has four notes,
every group also begins with the same stroke.
D-start groups: D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U ... through all 24 groups.
U-start groups: U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D ... through all 24 groups.
Never restart the pick cycle at a group, string crossing, octave root, turnaround, or frame shift.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Use sixteenth notes: one four-note group per beat. Begin 15-20 BPM below your clean Level 16
tempo. Master the ascending and descending A-major halves separately, then link them through
the repeated high-root turn. Use 2-3 neighboring rungs and pause one beat after each 96-note
cell. During the pause, release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both
pick starts. Then remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return to fret 5.
Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, an uneven group pulse,
dragged shift noise, a crossing accent, a B-string geometry error, or rising tension. Advance
after the full route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 18
MAJOR SCALE DIATONIC THIRDS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 18 leaves stepwise scale motion and begins intervallic sequencing. Each pair skips one scale degree:
1-3, 2-4, 3-5, and onward. After each upper note, the next pair rolls back one degree and continues upward.
The complete exercise retains the same two-octave six-string major-scale shape and one-fret chromatic neck route
used in Levels 13, 15, and 17.
MAIN SEQUENCE
INTERVAL-QUALITY PATTERN
Ascending:  M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3 | m3
Each pair is either a major third (M3 = 4 semitones) or minor third (m3 = 3 semitones).
The quality is determined by the major key, not by a fixed fret shape.
CELL DESIGN
- 13 ascending pairs / 26 notes
- repeat the high root at the turnaround
- 13 descending pairs / 26 notes
- 52 notes total per key
- shift the entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret only after the final 3-1 pair
PICKING
Downstroke start: D-U | D-U | D-U | ... through all 26 pairs.
Upstroke start:   U-D | U-D | U-D | ... through all 26 pairs.
Because every pair and the complete 52-note cell are even, every pair and every new key begins on the same
pick orientation. Do not reset at string changes, the middle octave, the repeated high root, or a new key.
RHYTHM
Learning pulse: one pair per beat as eighth notes.
Performance pulse: two pairs per beat as straight sixteenth notes.
Accent the first note of each pair while learning, then remove the accents and equalize all notes.
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. A major, first octave only: pairs 1-3 through 6-8, then reverse.
2. A major, all 13 ascending pairs.
3. A major, all 13 descending pairs.
4. Link the 52-note cell; articulate both high-root notes without resetting.
5. Use two or three neighboring keys with a one-beat pause only after each complete cell.
6. Remove the pause and complete the entire route with both pick starts.
CHROMATIC ROUTE
Up:   A -> Bb -> B -> C -> Db -> D -> Eb -> E -> F -> Gb -> G -> Ab -> A
Down: Ab -> G -> Gb -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> Db -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-major rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 19
MAJOR SCALE DIATONIC TRIADS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 19 stacks one more scale tone onto the diatonic-thirds idea from Level 18. Every group now plays
a root, third, and fifth: 1-3-5, 2-4-6, 3-5-7, and onward. The exercise converts the major scale into
a connected chain of broken triads while retaining the same two-octave six-string shape and one-fret route.
MAIN SEQUENCE
HARMONIC FUNCTION AND QUALITY
Ascending:  I major | ii minor | iii minor | IV major | V major | vi minor | vii diminished | I major | ii minor | iii minor | IV major
Descending: IV major | iii minor | ii minor | I major | vii diminished | vi minor | V major | IV major | iii minor | ii minor | I major
CELL DESIGN
- 11 ascending triads / 33 notes
- repeat the high root at the turnaround as the first note of the descending line
- 11 descending triads / 33 notes
- 22 triads / 66 notes total per key
- shift the entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret only after the final 5-3-1 triad
PICKING
Downstroke start: D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U ... through all 22 triads.
Upstroke start:   U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D ... through all 22 triads.
Every three-note triad flips the starting stroke of the next triad. The complete 66-note cell is even,
so every new key begins on the same pick orientation. Do not reset at group boundaries, string changes,
the middle octave, the repeated high root, or a new key.
RHYTHM
Learning pulse: one triad per beat as eighth-note triplets.
Performance pulse: two triads per beat as sixteenth-note triplets (sextuplets).
Accent the root of each triad while learning, then remove the accents and equalize every note.
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. A major, first octave only: 1-3-5 through 4-6-8, then reverse.
2. A major, all 11 ascending triads.
3. A major, all 11 descending triads.
4. Link the 66-note cell; articulate both high-root notes without resetting.
5. Use two or three neighboring keys with a one-beat pause only after each complete cell.
6. Remove the pause and complete the entire route with both pick starts.
CHROMATIC ROUTE
Up:   A -> Bb -> B -> C -> Db -> D -> Eb -> E -> F -> Gb -> G -> Ab -> A
Down: Ab -> G -> Gb -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> Db -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-major rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 20
MAJOR SCALE SYNTHESIS CIRCUIT - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 20 combines the established two-octave movements from Levels 13, 15, 17, 18, and 19 into
one uninterrupted major-scale circuit. Complete all five modules in the same key before shifting the
entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret. The low root is re-articulated at every module boundary.
FIVE-MODULE CELL
A. Linear scale:          30 notes - low root to high root, repeat high root, return to low root
B. Three-note roll:       78 notes - 13 ascending triplets and 13 descending triplets
C. Four-note roll:        96 notes - 12 ascending groups and 12 descending groups
D. Diatonic thirds:       52 notes - 13 ascending pairs and 13 descending pairs
E. Diatonic triads:       66 notes - 11 ascending triads and 11 descending triads
TOTAL:                   322 notes per key
MODULE ORDER
Linear -> Three-note roll -> Four-note roll -> Diatonic thirds -> Diatonic triads -> shift one fret
PICKING
All five module counts are even. With a downstroke start, every module and every new key begins on a
downstroke; with an upstroke start, each begins on an upstroke. Do not reset at group boundaries, string
changes, octave turns, module boundaries, or one-fret shifts.
RHYTHM
Learning mode: one note per metronome click through the complete circuit.
Native-pulse mode:
- Linear scale: 30 eighth notes = 15 beats
- Three-note roll: 78 triplet eighths = 26 beats
- Four-note roll: 96 sixteenth notes = 24 beats
- Diatonic thirds: 52 eighth notes = 26 beats
- Diatonic triads: 66 triplet eighths = 22 beats
TOTAL: 113 quarter-note beats per 322-note circuit
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Learn each module separately in A major.
2. Link adjacent module pairs: A-B, B-C, C-D, and D-E.
3. Play the complete A-major circuit with a short pause at each boundary.
4. Remove the pauses while retaining a light accent on each new module root.
5. Remove the accents and use two or three neighboring keys.
6. Complete longer route sections with both a downstroke and an upstroke start.
CHROMATIC ROUTE
Up:   A -> Bb -> B -> C -> Db -> D -> Eb -> E -> F -> Gb -> G -> Ab -> A
Down: Ab -> G -> Gb -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> Db -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-major rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.
ROUTE COUNT
25 circuits x 322 notes = 8,050 picked notes.
25 circuits x 113 native-pulse beats = 2,825 quarter-note beats.
The full route is a capstone endurance test, not a required daily warm-up.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 21
NATURAL MINOR ONE-FRET NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Learn one compact one-octave natural-minor shape, move the complete hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,
and repeat through every natural-minor key. Begin with A natural minor at low-E fret 5, climb to A natural
minor at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
PARALLEL MAJOR VS NATURAL MINOR
A major:         A B C# D E F# G# A
A natural minor: A B C  D E F  G  A
The 3rd, 6th, and 7th are each lowered one fret: 3 -> b3, 6 -> b6, 7 -> b7.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
Degrees:   1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole
COMPACT ONE-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3
The four-fret hand frame runs from R through R+3.
Ascending notes per string: 3-3-2. Descending notes per string: 2-3-3.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
Play degrees 1-2-b3-4-5-b6-b7-8, then 8-b7-b6-5-4-b3-2-1. The octave root is repeated at the turn.
This creates 16 notes, so the next key begins with the same alternate-picking orientation.
D-start: D U D U D U D U | D U D U D U D U
U-start: U D U D U D U D | U D U D U D U D
Do not restart the pick cycle at the scale turn or at the one-fret shift.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
First compare A major and A natural minor and identify the lowered 3rd, 6th, and 7th. Then use 3-4
neighboring natural-minor rungs. Play even eighth notes and pause one beat after each 16-note cell.
During the pause, release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts.
Then remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return to fret 5.
Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, dragged shift noise, or rising tension.
Advance after the complete route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

NATURAL MINOR TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Extend the Level 21 natural-minor shape across all six strings and two full octaves. Play the

and repeat through every natural-minor key. Begin with A natural minor at low-E fret 5, climb to A
natural minor at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A natural minor is the starting rung, not the key
of every rung. A fixed-key A-minor exercise in every neck position requires changing the note layout and
remains a separate later branch.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
Degrees:   1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7, repeated in the second octave
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole
TWO-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3
G string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4
B string:     R, R+1, R+3          Fingers 1,2,4
High e string:R                     Finger 1

frame relaxed, release pressure for the one-fret G-string backreach, and rebuild the hand for the B string.
STRING-DISTRIBUTION RULE
Ascending note counts by string: 3 - 3 - 2 - 3 - 3 - 1.
Descending note counts by string: 1 - 3 - 3 - 2 - 3 - 3.
The G string begins one fret below the root reference, and the B-string tuning offset changes the visible
pattern again. Use the assigned fingering rather than copying one string pattern onto the next.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
Ascend from the low root through the middle octave to the high root, repeat the high root at the turn,
then descend to the low root. The result is 30 notes, so the next key begins with the same pick orientation.
D-start: strict D-U alternate picking through every string crossing, the turn, and the one-fret relocation.
U-start: strict U-D alternate picking through every string crossing, the turn, and the one-fret relocation.
Do not restart the pick cycle on a new string, at either octave, at the scale turn, or after shifting one fret.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Begin 10-15 BPM below your clean Level 21 tempo. First master the A-natural-minor cell alone. Then use
2-3 neighboring rungs, play even eighth notes, and pause one beat after each 30-note cell while moving
the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts. Remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse
at fret 17, and return to fret 5. Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors,
string-crossing noise, dragged backreaches, or rising tension. Advance after the full route is clean with
both pick starts on two separate days.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 23
NATURAL MINOR THREE-NOTE ROLLING SEQUENCE - ONE-OCTAVE NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE

36-note up/down rolling cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,
and repeat through every natural-minor key. Begin with A natural minor at low-E fret 5, climb to A natural

PURPOSE

frame one fret. Re-articulate the low root at every module boundary while preserving the alternate-picking cycle.

MAJOR SCALE FOUR-NOTE ROLLING SEQUENCE - ONE-OCTAVE NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE

40-note up/down rolling cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb frame exactly
one fret, and repeat through every major key. Begin with A major at low-E fret 5, climb to
A major at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.

deliberately returns to the compact three-string octave so the new four-note overlap can be
learned without simultaneously managing the upper-octave B-string offset. Level 17 can extend
this exact sequence across the complete two-octave frame.

Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A major is the starting rung, not the
key of every rung. A fixed-key A-major exercise in every neck position requires changing the
note layout and remains a separate branch.

MAJOR SCALE DIATONIC THIRDS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 18 leaves stepwise scale motion and begins intervallic sequencing. Each pair skips one scale degree:
1-3, 2-4, 3-5, and onward. After each upper note, the next pair rolls back one degree and continues upward.
The complete exercise retains the same two-octave six-string major-scale shape and one-fret chromatic neck route

INTERVAL-QUALITY PATTERN

- repeat the high root at the turnaround
- 13 descending pairs / 26 notes

Upstroke start:   U-D | U-D | U-D | ... through all 26 pairs.

MAJOR SCALE SYNTHESIS CIRCUIT - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 20 combines the established two-octave movements from Levels 13, 15, 17, 18, and 19 into
one uninterrupted major-scale circuit. Complete all five modules in the same key before shifting the
entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret. The low root is re-articulated at every module boundary.
FIVE-MODULE CELL
A. Linear scale:          30 notes - low root to high root, repeat high root, return to low root
B. Three-note roll:       78 notes - 13 ascending triplets and 13 descending triplets
C. Four-note roll:        96 notes - 12 ascending groups and 12 descending groups
D. Diatonic thirds:       52 notes - 13 ascending pairs and 13 descending pairs
E. Diatonic triads:       66 notes - 11 ascending triads and 11 descending triads

Linear -> Three-note roll -> Four-note roll -> Diatonic thirds -> Diatonic triads -> shift one fret

downstroke; with an upstroke start, each begins on an upstroke. Do not reset at group boundaries, string
changes, octave turns, module boundaries, or one-fret shifts.

- Three-note roll: 78 triplet eighths = 26 beats
- Four-note roll: 96 sixteenth notes = 24 beats
- Diatonic thirds: 52 eighth notes = 26 beats

5. Remove the accents and use two or three neighboring keys.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 21
NATURAL MINOR ONE-FRET NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Learn one compact one-octave natural-minor shape, move the complete hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,
and repeat through every natural-minor key. Begin with A natural minor at low-E fret 5, climb to A natural
minor at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
PARALLEL MAJOR VS NATURAL MINOR
A major:         A B C# D E F# G# A
A natural minor: A B C  D E F  G  A
The 3rd, 6th, and 7th are each lowered one fret: 3 -> b3, 6 -> b6, 7 -> b7.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
Degrees:   1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole
COMPACT ONE-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3
The four-fret hand frame runs from R through R+3.
Ascending notes per string: 3-3-2. Descending notes per string: 2-3-3.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
Play degrees 1-2-b3-4-5-b6-b7-8, then 8-b7-b6-5-4-b3-2-1. The octave root is repeated at the turn.
This creates 16 notes, so the next key begins with the same alternate-picking orientation.
D-start: D U D U D U D U | D U D U D U D U
U-start: U D U D U D U D | U D U D U D U D
Do not restart the pick cycle at the scale turn or at the one-fret shift.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
First compare A major and A natural minor and identify the lowered 3rd, 6th, and 7th. Then use 3-4
neighboring natural-minor rungs. Play even eighth notes and pause one beat after each 16-note cell.
During the pause, release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts.
Then remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return to fret 5.
Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, dragged shift noise, or rising tension.
Advance after the complete route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

40-note up/down rolling cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,
and repeat through every natural-minor key. Begin with A natural minor at low-E fret 5, climb to A natural
minor at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
WHY THIS LEVEL RETURNS TO ONE OCTAVE
Level 24 expanded the three-note rolling sequence across two octaves and all six strings. Level 25
deliberately returns to the compact three-string octave so the new four-note overlap can be learned without
simultaneously managing the upper-octave backreach and B-string offset. Level 26 will extend this exact
sequence across the complete two-octave frame.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A natural minor is the starting rung, not the key of every rung.
A fixed-key A-natural-minor exercise in every neck position requires changing the note layout and remains a separate branch.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA

Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole

A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4

third and then continues forward. Three notes overlap from one group to the next. Do not pause, accent,
or reset at a group boundary.

the last note of 5-b6-b7-8 is followed by the first note of 8-b7-b6-5. Because 40 is even, the next
key begins with the same pick orientation. Because every group has four notes, every group also begins
with the same stroke.

U-start groups: U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D ... through all 10 groups.

NATURAL MINOR DIATONIC THIRDS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 27 leaves stepwise and rolling natural-minor motion and begins intervallic sequencing.
Each pair skips one scale degree: 1-b3, 2-4, b3-5, and onward. After each upper note,
the next pair rolls back one degree and continues upward. The exercise retains the same
two-octave six-string natural-minor shape and one-fret chromatic neck route used in Levels
WHAT CHANGES FROM LEVEL 26
Level 26 moved in overlapping four-note scale fragments. Level 27 replaces those fragments
with two-note diatonic thirds. The mechanical demand is shorter, but the musical demand is
higher: hear whether each pair is a minor third or major third, preserve the one-degree
rollback, and keep every string crossing inside one uninterrupted line.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
One octave: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Two octaves: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8 9 b10 11 12 b13 b14 15
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole, then repeat
MAIN SEQUENCE
Each new pair begins one scale position farther forward. Between pairs, the line rolls back
one degree: 1-b3 then 2-4; 4-b6 then 5-b7. Do not pause or reset at the rollback.
INTERVAL-QUALITY PATTERN
Ascending:  m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3
Descending: M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3
M3 = major third = 4 semitones. m3 = minor third = 3 semitones.
First-octave natural-minor pattern: m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3.
Natural minor uses the same two third sizes as major, but the order begins differently.

Descending: eB | BB | BG | BG | GG | GD | GD | DA | DA | AA | AE | AE | EE

- 13 descending pairs / 26 notes

repeated high root, or a new key.

Learning pulse: one pair per beat as eighth notes.
Performance pulse: two pairs per beat as straight sixteenth notes.

PURPOSE
Level 28 stacks one more scale tone onto the diatonic-thirds idea from Level 27. Every group now plays
a root, third, and fifth: 1-b3-5, 2-4-b6, b3-5-b7, and onward. The exercise converts natural
minor into a connected chain of broken triads while retaining the same two-octave six-string shape
and one-fret chromatic neck route.
WHAT CHANGES FROM LEVEL 27
Level 27 isolated two-note thirds and their major/minor qualities. Level 28 adds the diatonic fifth,
turning every interval pair into a complete triad. The mechanical demand becomes a three-note group
that may span one, two, or three strings; the musical demand is to hear and name i, ii diminished,
III, iv, v, VI, and VII without losing the continuous triplet pulse.

Each new triad begins one scale position farther forward. The line climbs a third and another third,
then rolls back three scale positions to begin the next chord. Do not pause or reset at the rollback.

Ascending:  i minor | ii diminished | III major | iv minor | v minor | VI major | VII major | i minor | ii diminished | III major | iv minor
Descending: iv minor | III major | ii diminished | i minor | VII major | VI major | v minor | iv minor | III major | ii diminished | i minor

those functions later; do not import the raised seventh into this workbook.
